main_body: Tall brick shop-house facade: slate mansard roof with two dormers and a chimney, an orange cornice, two floors of windows, a balcony, a striped awning and a shopfront.
top_band: Column through the middle: rows 10-26 teal-grey roof panel, rows 27-42 blue-grey slate slope with dormers, rows 43-46 orange cornice, then the brick front face from row 47. The roof is a steep front-facing slope with no clear horizontal top surface seen from above.
evidence: The main volume is the brick wall with windows, a balcony and a shopfront, all drawn face-on as vertical faces. The mansard slate reads as another vertical front panel, not a foreshortened top. The orange cornice is only a 3-4 row band. The windows are flat with light frames and no inset shadow. The reference houses show real roof planes above their walls, and this has none. It is a front elevation with a roof-like hat, so it fails.

style.evidence: Brick has several red-brown tones with mortar variation. The slate has per-tile variation. The lit windows carry speckled orange and yellow dots. Outlines are dark brown, blue-grey or red-brown beside their materials rather than black. The awning, balcony railing and storefront are detailed. Information density per tile is at least as high as the Beodeul houses, so it would sit next to the reference without looking thinner.
